satirical_subtitle: Synergizing the Paradigm One WordArt at a Time

quest_giver.location_detail: Velvet Curtain Club, near the bar
quest_giver.trigger_text: Bros visit Velvet Curtain Club after previous quests

satirical_targets: Primary Target: People who peaked in the early 2000s and never updated their skills
Secondary Targets: Outdated slang, Y2K aesthetic nostalgia, "guru" marketing speak, nu-metal era masculinity
Cultural Specificity: American tourists assuming their approach translates everywhere
Y2K/Era References: GeoCities, WordArt, Hotmail, AIM, Friendster, Kazaa, "synergy"

dialogue.speaker: Vape Witch Vanessa
dialogue.line: You three. You look like you know how to... hustle. DJ Beatdrop needs promotion. Rival DJ Hardstyle Hynek is trying to steal his Thursday night slot. I need someone to poster the city. 100 SOVS, plus free drinks tonight.

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: Lady, you just hired the right team. I was a MARKETING MAJOR.

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: I have 47 ICQ contacts. I know how to go viral.

dialogue.speaker: Bradley
dialogue.line: I once made a website with frames AND a visitor counter. It got 47 hits.

dialogue.speaker: Vanessa
dialogue.line: Just... put up the flyers. DJ Beatdrop. Thursday. Velvet Curtain Club.

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: Oh, we're gonna do more than that. We're gonna SYNERGIZE this whole paradigm.

dialogue.speaker: Vanessa
dialogue.line: Please don't.

dialogue.direction: Bros gather at hostel with borrowed laptop

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: Okay, first we need to establish our brand identity. What says 'cool DJ' to a Euromemeian audience?

dialogue.speaker: Bradley
dialogue.line: Flames. Flames are universal.

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: And we need an email so people can RSVP. I'll set one up.

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: beatdrop_promo@hotmail.com is available.

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: PERFECT. Now THAT'S professional.

dialogue.speaker: Bradley
dialogue.line: I'm adding our contact info. My ICQ number is 48291057. Chadwick?

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: 72845619. Also add my AIM: SocialMediaGuru02.

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: This is coming together. Now we need VISUALS.

quest_stages.name: the_flyer_creation
flyer_design_elements: WordArt title: "DJ BEATDROP" in rainbow gradient with shadow
Dancing baby GIF (printed as static image)
Spinning envelope icon next to email (static)
Their ICQ numbers AND AIM handles
"All That and a Bag of Chips!" tagline
"Click Here for FREE RINGTONES" (non-functional, on paper)
QR codes that just link to their dead Friendster profiles

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: This is clean. This is PROFESSIONAL. DJ Beatdrop is gonna love this.

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: Should I add my Friendster profile link?

dialogue.speaker: Bradley
dialogue.line: Friendster might be too exclusive. Keep it accessible. Just the Hotmail.

quest_stages.name: web_1_0_marketing_mastery
quest_stages.description: Bros poster the city with their GeoCities-era flyers
execution: Poster Astronomical Cock-Up Square (near the clock)
Bradley suggests SEO optimization (on paper flyers)

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: Placement is key. Eye level. Where the DECISION MAKERS will see it.

dialogue.direction: Local walks by, looks at flyer, stops

dialogue.speaker: Local
dialogue.line: Is this... is this performance art? Are you mocking early internet?

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: This is PROFESSIONAL MARKETING. American style.

dialogue.speaker: Local
dialogue.line: This is the most beautiful thing I've ever seen. My design professor needs to see this.

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: Chat, we're doing real guerrilla marketing right now. This is how you build a brand organically.

dialogue.direction: No one is watching his stream. Zero viewers.

dialogue.speaker: Arcade Employee
dialogue.line: Dude. Did you make this on Microsoft Publisher?

dialogue.speaker: Bradley
dialogue.line: Publisher PREMIUM.

dialogue.speaker: Arcade Employee
dialogue.line: My mom used this font in 2002. For my birthday invitations.

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: Your mom sounds like she had great taste.

dialogue.speaker: Bradley
dialogue.line: Here you go, ma'am. DJ Beatdrop. Thursday. Tell your friends.

dialogue.speaker: Elderly Local
dialogue.line: What is... 'All That and a Bag of Chips'?

dialogue.speaker: Bradley
dialogue.line: It means it's going to be... off the hook.

dialogue.speaker: Elderly Local
dialogue.line: Is there a phone number? I only see numbers with letters.

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: That's our ICQ. You message us there.

dialogue.speaker: Elderly Local
dialogue.line: What is an ICQ?

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: These people aren't ready for American marketing.

npc_reactions.speaker: Art Student
npc_reactions.line: This is brilliant commentary on Y2K aesthetic nostalgia and the death of Web 1.0 visual language... wait, you're SERIOUS?

npc_reactions.speaker: Club Regular
npc_reactions.line: I'm framing this. My apartment has an ironic 2000s corner. This is perfect.

npc_reactions.speaker: DJ Beatdrop
npc_reactions.line: What the f--- ...actually, you know what? People are talking about it. That's... something.

npc_reactions.speaker: Hipster Collecting Them
npc_reactions.line: These are authentic Y2K memorabilia. I'll pay 5 SOVS each.

quest_stages.name: alpha_male_vandalism_2001
quest_stages.description: Bros decide to sabotage rival DJ Hardstyle Hynek instead
execution: Draw flame decals over his face
Add tribal tattoo designs over venue information
Bradley writes "All Your Base Are Belong to Us" thinking it's current
Lord Pilsner adds beer bottle stickers to Hynek's face
Bradley crosses out names and writes "THIS SUCKS" in block letters
Gel pens and correction fluid deployed like weapons of mass destruction
y2k_cringe_details: Add tribal tattoo designs copied from nu-metal album covers

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: New plan. We don't just PROMOTE Beatdrop. We DESTROY Hynek.

dialogue.speaker: Bradley
dialogue.line: Negative advertising. Bold. Disruptive.

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: I brought gel pens.

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.direction: adding flame decals with red gel pen
dialogue.line: You see this? This is psychological warfare.

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: P-W-N-E-D. Get rekt, Hynek.

dialogue.speaker: Bradley
dialogue.line: I'm adding a tribal sun. It represents his career... setting.

dialogue.speaker: Security Guard
dialogue.line: Are you the guys who've been writing 'BOOYAH!' on everything?

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: That's proprietary marketing. You can't prove anything.

dialogue.speaker: Security Guard
dialogue.direction: gestures at Chadwick still holding gel pen over flyer

dialogue.speaker: Chadwick
dialogue.line: ...this isn't what it looks like?

dialogue.direction: Local Graffiti Artist sees their work

dialogue.speaker: Graffiti Artist
dialogue.line: Yo, did some American tourists escape from a time machine?

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: This is GUERRILLA marketing. Look it up.

dialogue.speaker: Graffiti Artist
dialogue.line: Bro, I'm gonna add 'CIRCA 2001' labels to all of these. For historical accuracy.

dialogue.direction: He does. The defaced flyers become an ironic art installation.

dialogue.speaker: Club Regular
dialogue.line: My little brother drew better stuff than this... in 2003.

dialogue.speaker: Hynek
dialogue.line: SOMEONE wrote 'ALL YOUR BASE ARE BELONG TO US' on my promotional materials.

dialogue.speaker: Hynek
dialogue.line: And 'WASSSUUUUP!' with like... six U's.

dialogue.speaker: Lord Pilsner
dialogue.line: Psychological. Warfare.

dialogue.speaker: Hynek
dialogue.line: But weirdly, people are coming to see who did it. They think it's an art project?
